St. John the Dwarf

St. John the Dwarf

St. John the Short · St. John Kolobos · St. Abba John the Dwarf

Period
Fifth-century ascetic life in the cited OCA entry; exact dates not supplied
Region
Egypt; Scetis
Titles / vocation
Monastic
Commemoration
November 9

Introduction

An Egyptian Desert Father also called St. John the Short. His received stories emphasize humility, work, obedience, and the guidance of other monks.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomTeaching and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Death date and circumstances are not given in the cited entry

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The OCA places St. John’s desert ascetic life in fifth-century Egypt and relates that he entered monastic life with his brother. His epithet distinguishes this St. John from other saints of the same name.

[1] Official Orthodox life · Opening paragraph

Life and notable events

One story contrasts his wish to live without bodily necessities with his return hungry to the community. Another describes the long watering of dry wood that finally bears fruit. These are transmitted monastic teaching narratives, not a new prayer rule for readers.

[1] Official Orthodox life · Narratives of the return and the dry stick

Death and martyrdom

The cited entry gives no death date or circumstances. It commemorates him as a venerable monk without narrating a martyrdom.

[1] Official Orthodox life · Complete entry and heading

Teaching and legacy

John became a spiritual guide. The OCA’s life of Saint Arsenius the Great recounts how John received the former courtier, tested his humility, and accepted him into monastic life.

[2] Official Orthodox life · Paragraphs on Arsenius’s arrival and reception by Abba John

Chronology

  1. Fifth century

    Period of his Egyptian desert life in the OCA account.
